note.summary: Live price and gain/loss data were not provided for Intel (INTC), so the position's current P&L cannot be stated. The posts are mostly neutral-to-positive: Intel's 14A PDK 0.9 release, day-zero support for Meta's Muse Spark model, and a Diamond Rapids motherboard showing.
note.what_changed: Nothing new in the posts touching the report's named risks around backside power, buried rails, or failure analysis. New items are product/process progress signals (14A PDK 0.9, GPU D-series/Xeon model support, Diamond Rapids hardware) plus general memory-capacity and China-memory commentary that does not name Intel specifically.
risks: Posts say memory capacity is being stretched by HBM demand with rising memory costs, which could reshape hardware economics Intel depends on.
Report risks stand: unresolved backside/buried power metal choice (Ru vs Mo) and failure-analysis bottlenecks for backside architectures.
China memory competition commentary (posts say, unverified) adds an uncertain competitive backdrop.
